sentences.text: Heard Mr. D.P. Goswami, learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Assam.

Learned Additional Public Prosecutor has raised objection stating that although through the additional affidavit the petitioner has submitted that the vehicle in dispute has been returned on 04.03.2022, yet the charge sheet was laid against the petitioner on 30.11.2023.

3. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that an agreement was executed between the petitioner and the respondent No. 2 in the year 2022 and the allegation against the petitioner is that the petitioner had hired the vehicle from the respondent No. 2 for monthly payment of rent of Rs.1,20,000/- (Rupees One Lac and Twenty Thousand) for one year but he failed to pay the hired charges in time and he also did not return the vehicle, which is a JCB excavator bearing registration No. AS19AC2671.

It is further alleged that the vehicle was kept for an extended period of four months and the informant was paid Rs.7,74,500/- (Rupees Seven Lacs Seventy Four Thousand and Five Hundred) while the entire amount was misappropriated by the petitioner who has refused to return the balance amount and has blocked the calls of respondent No. 2.

It is further submitted that this is a civil dispute in the garb of a criminal case and there are several guidelines of the Hon'ble Supreme Court not to proceed in criminal cases which are brought up instead of taking recourse to a civil Court.

4. The petitioner has drawn the attention of this Court to the work order Page No.# 3/4 marked as Anneuxre-3 of this petition and on the basis of this work order, the aforementioned vehicle was hired way back on 30.10.2020 whereas the FIR was lodged in the year 2023 and clause 15 of the work order reflects that the dispute falls under the jurisdiction of Courts at Guwahati, which implies that the criminal case was erroneously proceeded upon by the Court at Bongaigaon.

5. The petitioner has further drawn the attention of this Court to the Anticipatory Bail order dated 07.11.2023 passed by a Coordinate Bench of this Court in connection with AB No. 3113/2023,
wherein the petitioner was granted anticipatory bail as no prima facie case was found against the petitioner.
6. It appears that further proceeding of PRC Case No. 151/2024 may be stayed.

7. Call for the scanned copies of the Trial Court Records along with the scanned copies of the Case Diary.
8.
Petitioner to take steps to issue notice to respondent No. 2 as per usual process, returnable within four weeks.

9. Meanwhile, further proceeding of the PRC Case No. 151/2024 arising out of Bongaigaon Police Station Case No. 363/2023, pending in the Court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Bongaigaon, is stayed until further orders.
10. List accordingly.
